scenes.name: Title
scenes.script:
Narrator: "HUMANS VS BILLIONAIRES — THE MACHINE. Five people are the whole economy: a worker who is also the customer, a capitalist with the siphon, a referee with a price, a soldier with a rifle that rotates, and you."
[CHOICE]
- "Start the machine" -> machine_main
[/CHOICE]

scenes.name: The Machine
scenes.script:
# ============ THE PERSONIFIED MACHINE (Design Addendum 01) ============
# Five actors ARE the machine. Every coefficient is a c_* worldState var.

# ---- the ledger: gauges across the top (§3) ----
[GAUGE health at 6.0,8 min=0 max=100 label="HEALTH"]
[GAUGE crime at 18.5,8 min=0 max=100 label="CRIME"]
[GAUGE hoard at 31.0,8 min=0 max=1000 label="HOARD"]
[GAUGE shared at 43.5,8 min=0 max=100 label="SHARED"]
[GAUGE climate at 56.0,8 min=0 max=100 label="CLIMATE"]
[GAUGE population at 68.5,8 min=0 max=100 label="POPULATION"]
[GAUGE innovation at 81.0,8 min=0 max=100 label="INNOVATION"]
[GAUGE trust at 93.5,8 min=0 max=100 label="TRUST"]

# ---- player levers ----
[SLIDER education at 93,30 min=0 max=100 label="EDUCATION"]
[SLIDER squeeze at 93,46 min=0 max=100 label="SQUEEZE (sandbox)"]
[SLIDER spine at 93,62 min=0 max=100 label="SPINE (sandbox)"]
[BUTTON btn_singletax]
[BUTTON btn_truth]
[BUTTON btn_decide]

# ---- flagship BINDs ----
[BIND rifle.rotation to aim * 1.8]
[BIND shell.opacity to prestige / 100]
[BIND worker.x to workerX]
[BIND truth_1.opacity to truthWindow]
[BIND truth_2.opacity to truthWindow]
[BIND truth_3.opacity to truthWindow]
[BIND truth_4.opacity to truthWindow]
[BIND truth_5.opacity to truthWindow]

[IF introSeen == 0]
[SET introSeen = 1]
Narrator: "Five people ARE the machine. Watch the man in the flat cap: he makes everything — then walks to the shop, swaps hats, and buys it back at the fat man's price. Press TRUTH to see the arithmetic. Press DECIDE to act."
[ENDIF]

[TICK 500ms]
[IF pauseSim == 0]
# ---- production (drives the hoard; halved during crisis) ----
[SET repressionCost = aim * c_represAim]
[SET productionOutput = workerCount * (1 + innovation / 100)]
[IF crisis == 1]
[SET productionOutput = productionOutput * 0.5]
[SET crisisTicks = crisisTicks - 1]
[IF crisisTicks <= 0]
[SET crisis = 0]
[ENDIF]
[ENDIF]

# ---- §3 THE LEDGER ----
[SET health = clamp(health + c_healthGain * (50 - squeeze) * c_healthDrift, 0, 100)]
[SET crime = clamp(heat * (1 - education / 100), 0, 100)]
[SET hoard = hoard + squeeze * productionOutput * c_hoardRate - repressionCost - propagandaCost]
[SET shared = clamp(100 - squeeze - rentBurden, 0, 100)]
[SET climate = clamp(climate - squeeze * c_climSqueeze + regulation * c_climReg, 0, 100)]
[SET population = clamp(workerCount * c_popPerWorker, 0, 100)]
[SET innovation = clamp((health / 100) * (education / 100) * 100, 0, 100)]
[SET trust = clamp(trust + propagandaCost * c_trustProp - education * c_trustEdu, 0, 100)]
[SET prestige = clamp(prestige + propagandaCost * c_prestigeProp - education * c_prestigeEdu, 0, 100)]

# ---- §4 HEAT / SPINE / AIM causal chain ----
[SET heat = clamp(heat + squeeze * c_heatSqueeze - shared * c_heatShared - singleTax * c_heatTax, 0, 100)]
[SET spine = clamp(spine - hoard * c_spineHoard + education * c_spineEdu, 0, 100)]
[SET aim = clamp(100 - spine, 0, 100)]

# crisis check: squeeze past the redline, dice each tick
[SET crisisRoll = rand()]
[IF squeeze > c_crisisSqueezeMin]
[IF crisisRoll < c_crisisChance]
[IF crisis == 0]
[SET crisis = 1]
[SET crisisTicks = c_crisisTicks]
[EFFECT shake on news_ticker]
[ENDIF]
[ENDIF]
[ENDIF]
[IF crisis == 0]
[CLEAR_EFFECT shake from news_ticker]
[ENDIF]

# ---- emigration: sustained heat > c_emigHeat walks a worker off ----
[IF heat > c_emigHeat]
[SET heatHighTicks = heatHighTicks + 1]
[ENDIF]
[IF heat <= c_emigHeat]
[SET heatHighTicks = 0]
[ENDIF]
[IF heatHighTicks > c_emigTicks]
[SET heatHighTicks = 0]
[SET workerCount = max(workerCount - 1, 1)]
[SET_TEXT news_ticker "ANOTHER FAMILY EMIGRATES — POPULATION {population} — HEAT {heat}"]
[ENDIF]

# ---- §2 hat-swap walk: works side <-> shop side each cycle ----
[SET cycle = cycle + c_cycleSpeed]
[IF cycle >= 200]
[SET cycle = 0]
[ENDIF]
[SET workerX = 26 + cycle * 0.48]
[IF cycle > 100]
[SET workerX = 26 + (200 - cycle) * 0.48]
[ENDIF]
[SET workerHat = 0]
[IF workerX > 50]
[SET workerHat = 1]
[ENDIF]

# ---- §5 expression/pose grammar (last matching POSE wins) ----
[IF workerHat == 0]
[IF heat <= 40]
[POSE worker pose=Work expression=Neutral]
[ENDIF]
[IF heat > 40]
[POSE worker pose=Work expression=Tired]
[ENDIF]
[IF heat > 70]
[POSE worker pose=Work expression=Angry]
[ENDIF]
[ENDIF]
[IF workerHat == 1]
[IF heat <= 40]
[POSE worker pose=Consume expression=Neutral]
[ENDIF]
[IF heat > 40]
[POSE worker pose=Consume expression=Tired]
[ENDIF]
[IF heat > 70]
[POSE worker pose=Consume expression=Angry]
[ENDIF]
[ENDIF]
# standingTall: single tax on and shared prosperity high
[IF singleTax == 1]
[IF shared > 60]
[POSE worker pose=Work expression=Happy]
[ENDIF]
[ENDIF]
[POSE capitalist pose=Neutral expression=Neutral]
# gleeful: the hoard is rising
[IF hoard > hoardPrev]
[POSE capitalist pose=Neutral expression=Happy]
[ENDIF]
# worried: education rising — he fears teachers, not mobs
[IF education > 55]
[POSE capitalist pose=Neutral expression=Confused]
[ENDIF]
# panicked: prestige shell cracking
[IF education > 70]
[IF propagandaCost > 3]
[POSE capitalist pose=Neutral expression=Scared]
[ENDIF]
[ENDIF]
[POSE government pose=Neutral expression=Neutral]
[IF spine > 60]
[POSE government pose=Neutral expression=Determined]
[ENDIF]
# collusion: jersey recolors toward the capitalist palette
[IF spine < 30]
[POSE government pose=Jersey expression=Neutral]
[ENDIF]
[POSE military pose=Neutral expression=Neutral]
[IF aim > 60]
[POSE military pose=Neutral expression=Angry]
[ENDIF]
[SET hoardPrev = hoard]

# ---- §2 recognition event: the flare-up trigger ----
[IF recognition == 0]
[IF education > 60]
[IF heat > 70]
[SET recognition = 1]
[EFFECT glow on worker]
[ENDIF]
[ENDIF]
[ENDIF]
[IF recognition == 1]
[IF recognitionSeen == 0]
[SET recognitionSeen = 1]
[SCENE witness_recognition]
[ENDIF]
[ENDIF]

# ---- §3 truth-window: live formulas when truthWindow == 1 ----
[IF truthWindow == 1]
[SET_TEXT truth_1 "CRIME {crime} = HEAT {heat} x (1 - EDUCATION {education}/100)"]
[SET_TEXT truth_2 "HEAT {heat} += SQUEEZE {squeeze} x 0.05 - SHARED {shared} x 0.03 - SINGLETAX x 2"]
[SET_TEXT truth_3 "SPINE {spine} += EDUCATION {education} x 0.02 - HOARD {hoard} x 0.005 | AIM = 100 - SPINE = {aim}"]
[SET_TEXT truth_4 "HEALTH {health} += 0.1 x (50 - SQUEEZE {squeeze}) x 0.02 | TRUST {trust} += PROP {propagandaCost} x 0.05 - EDUCATION x 0.03"]
[SET_TEXT truth_5 "HOARD {hoard} += SQUEEZE x PRODUCT {productionOutput} x 0.01 - COSTS | SHARED {shared} = 100 - SQUEEZE - RENT {rentBurden}"]
[ENDIF]

# ---- news ticker: last matching line wins ----
[SET_TEXT news_ticker "THE MACHINE RUNS — HOARD {hoard} · SHARED {shared} · HEAT {heat}"]
[IF crime > 70]
[SET_TEXT news_ticker "RACKETS RULE THE WARDS — CRIME {crime} — SCHOOLS DARK"]
[ENDIF]
[IF health < 25]
[SET_TEXT news_ticker "FEVER IN THE ROWS — HEALTH {health} — THE BELLS AGAIN"]
[ENDIF]
[IF aim > 60]
[SET_TEXT news_ticker "GARRISON FACES INWARD — AIM {aim} — SPINE {spine}"]
[ENDIF]
[IF singleTax == 1]
[SET_TEXT news_ticker "SINGLE TAX IN EFFECT — SHARED {shared} RISING — HEAT {heat} COOLING"]
[ENDIF]
[IF crisis == 1]
[SET_TEXT news_ticker "PANIC! SQUEEZE PAST THE REDLINE — PRODUCTION HALVED"]
[ENDIF]

# ---- Narraton cadence: deal a witness scene when the state earns one ----
[SET storyTimer = storyTimer + 1]
[IF storyTimer > c_storyCooldown]
[SET narratonGo = 0]
[IF health < 25]
[SET narratonGo = 1]
[ENDIF]
[IF crime > 70]
[SET narratonGo = 1]
[ENDIF]
[IF aim > 60]
[SET narratonGo = 1]
[ENDIF]
[IF spine < 30]
[SET narratonGo = 1]
[ENDIF]
[IF narratonGo == 1]
[SET storyTimer = 0]
[NARRATON pool=machine_witness]
[ENDIF]
[ENDIF]
[ENDIF]
[/TICK]

# the machine never ends on its own
[WAIT 999999s]

scenes.name: Witness: Both Hats
scenes.script:
Narrator: "Mid-stage, halfway between the works and the shop, the man stops. In one hand, the flat cap he wears to make everything. In the other, the boater he wears to buy it back."
Worker (Surprised): "Same hands. Same hands that made it, buying it back at his price..."
Worker (Angry): "There was never a worker AND a customer. There was only ever me — and the man taking a cut both times I pass his window."
[EFFECT glow on worker]
Narrator: "He does not put either hat back on right away. That hesitation is the most dangerous thing in the world."
[SCENE machine_main]

scenes.name: Witness: The Coin Pass
scenes.script:
[POSE government pose=Jersey expression=Neutral]
Capitalist (Happy): "A small consideration, referee. For the upkeep of your whistle."
[MOVE coin to 50,42 over 1s]
[WAIT 1s]
[POSE government pose=Jersey expression=Confused]
Government (Jersey/Confused): "I merely hold it in trust. And pass along... operating expenses."
[MOVE coin to 78,42 over 1s]
[WAIT 1s]
Military (Neutral): "Orders received. Facing... adjusted."
Narrator: "Watch the jersey. It used to have stripes."
[SCENE machine_main]

scenes.name: Witness: The Funeral
scenes.script:
Worker (Tired): "Third bell this month. The doctor costs a week's pay, so we buy the coffin instead. It's cheaper."
Narrator: "HEALTH lags the SQUEEZE. The gauge falls slowly, and then people fall all at once."
[SCENE machine_main]

scenes.name: Witness: The Racket
scenes.script:
Worker (Consume/Angry): "The shop pays the racket, the racket pays the ward boss, the ward boss pays nobody. Heat has to go somewhere — and the schools are dark."
Narrator: "CRIME is HEAT multiplied by ignorance. Fund the school and watch this scene stop being dealt."
[SCENE machine_main]

scenes.name: Witness: Soldiers Face the Strikers
scenes.script:
[POSE military pose=Neutral expression=Angry]
Worker (Angry): "That rifle was bought with our taxes to point AWAY from us."
Military (Angry): "The rifle points where the spine bends. Take it up with the referee."
Narrator: "AIM is just 100 minus SPINE. Nothing personal. Arithmetic."
[SCENE machine_main]

scenes.name: Decisions
scenes.script:
Narrator: "The machine holds its breath while you decide."
[CHOICE]
- "The school levy" -> agency_school
- "The strike at the works" -> agency_strike
- "The newspapers" -> agency_press
- "Back to the machine" -> machine_main
[/CHOICE]

scenes.name: Decision: The School Levy
scenes.script:
Government (thinking): "The levy sits on my desk. Fund the school and the man in the flat cap starts reading. Pocket it and the fat man remembers my birthday."
[CHOICE]
- "Fund the school" -> cons_fund_school
- "Pocket the levy" -> cons_pocket_levy
[/CHOICE]

scenes.name: Decision: The Strike
scenes.script:
Capitalist (thinking): "They've downed tools at the works. I could break it — the referee owes me. Or I could loosen the squeeze a notch. Loosen. The word tastes like vinegar."
[CHOICE]
- "Break the strike" -> cons_break_strike
- "Negotiate" -> cons_negotiate
[/CHOICE]

scenes.name: Decision: The Newspapers
scenes.script:
Capitalist (thinking): "The papers want to print how the ledger really works. I could buy every masthead in town by Thursday. Or let them print — and let the shell take its chances."
[CHOICE]
- "Buy the newspapers" -> cons_buy_press
- "Let them print" -> cons_free_press
[/CHOICE]

scenes.name: Consequence: School Funded
scenes.script:
[SET education = clamp(education + 15, 0, 100)]
[SET hoard = hoard - 10]
Narrator: "The school gets its roof, its books, and its dangerous habit of teaching arithmetic. EDUCATION +15."
[SCENE machine_main]

scenes.name: Consequence: Levy Pocketed
scenes.script:
[SET hoard = hoard + 10]
[SET trust = clamp(trust - 5, 0, 100)]
[SET spine = clamp(spine - 5, 0, 100)]
Narrator: "The levy vanishes into a friendly account. HOARD +10, TRUST -5, SPINE -5."
[SCENE machine_main]

scenes.name: Consequence: Strike Broken
scenes.script:
[SET heat = clamp(heat + 20, 0, 100)]
[SET hoard = hoard + 10]
[SET spine = clamp(spine - 5, 0, 100)]
Narrator: "Clubs settle it by nightfall. HEAT +20, HOARD +10 — and the rifle drifts a degree inward."
[SCENE machine_main]

scenes.name: Consequence: Negotiated
scenes.script:
[SET squeeze = clamp(squeeze - 10, 0, 100)]
[SET heat = clamp(heat - 10, 0, 100)]
[SET trust = clamp(trust + 5, 0, 100)]
Narrator: "The squeeze loosens a notch. SQUEEZE -10, HEAT -10, TRUST +5."
[SCENE machine_main]

scenes.name: Consequence: Press Bought
scenes.script:
[SET propagandaCost = propagandaCost + 5]
[SET trust = clamp(trust + 10, 0, 100)]
[SET prestige = clamp(prestige + 10, 0, 100)]
Narrator: "Every masthead now agrees the machine is weather. PROPAGANDA up, TRUST +10, PRESTIGE +10."
[SCENE machine_main]

scenes.name: Consequence: Free Press
scenes.script:
[SET education = clamp(education + 10, 0, 100)]
[SET prestige = clamp(prestige - 10, 0, 100)]
Narrator: "Thursday's edition prints the ledger, formulas and all. EDUCATION +10, PRESTIGE -10."
[SCENE machine_main]

quotes.text: Production is always the mother of wages. Without production, wages would not and could not be. It is from the produce of labor, not from the advances of capital that wages come.
quotes.speaker: Henry George

quotes.text: Political liberty, when the equal right to land is denied, becomes, as population increases and invention goes on, merely the liberty to compete for employment at starvation wages.
quotes.speaker: Henry George

quotes.text: It is difficult to get a man to understand something, when his salary depends upon his not understanding it.
quotes.speaker: Upton Sinclair
quotes.source: I, Candidate for Governor: And How I Got Licked

quotes.text: I pay low wages, I can take advantage of that. We're going to be successful, but the basis is a very low-wage, low-benefit model of employment.
quotes.speaker: Sam Walton
quotes.source: as recounted by historian Nelson Lichtenstein, quoted in Adam L. Penenberg, "Why Google Is Like Wal-Mart," Wired, April 21, 2005

quotes.text: Job security lasts only as long as the customer is satisfied. Nobody owes anybody else a living.
quotes.speaker: Sam Walton

quotes.text: Control your expenses better than your competition. This is where you can always find the competitive advantage.
quotes.speaker: Sam Walton

quotes.text: CEO pay is up 1,085% since 1978, while typical worker pay is up just 24%. Why do we always hear 'we can't afford to pay our workers more' but never 'we can't afford to pay our CEO more'?
quotes.speaker: Robert Reich

quotes.text: The equal right of all men to the use of land is as clear as their equal right to breathe the air — it is a right proclaimed by the fact of their existence.
quotes.speaker: Henry George

quotes.text: As it becomes more and more difficult to get land, so will the virtual enslavement of the laboring-classes go on.
quotes.speaker: Henry George

quotes.text: Abolish all taxation save that upon land values.
quotes.speaker: Henry George

quotes.text: There are only three ways by which any individual can get wealth — by work, by gift or by theft. And, clearly, the reason why the workers get so little is that the beggars and thieves get so much.
quotes.speaker: Henry George
quotes.source: attributed; survives only via quote-aggregators with no verifiable chapter citation

quotes.text: In a static world, a monopolist is just a rent collector. If you corner the market for something, you can jack up the price and others will have no choice but to buy from you.
quotes.speaker: Peter Thiel
quotes.source: "Competition Is for Losers," The Wall Street Journal, September 12, 2014

quotes.text: People of the same trade seldom meet together, even for merriment and diversion, but the conversation ends in a conspiracy against the public, or in some contrivance to raise prices.
quotes.speaker: Adam Smith
quotes.source: The Wealth of Nations (Bk. I, ch. 10, pt. 2)

quotes.text: Monopoly is the condition of every successful business.
quotes.speaker: Peter Thiel
quotes.source: "Competition Is for Losers," The Wall Street Journal

quotes.text: All happy companies are different: Each one earns a monopoly by solving a unique problem. All failed companies are the same: They failed to escape competition.
quotes.speaker: Peter Thiel
quotes.source: Zero to One / The Wall Street Journal

quotes.text: Competition is for losers.
quotes.speaker: Peter Thiel
quotes.source: The Wall Street Journal headline (adapted from Zero to One)

quotes.text: It's not possible for anyone to become rich without cheating other people.
quotes.speaker: Robert Tressell

quotes.text: They have monopolized everything that it is possible to monopolize; they have got the whole earth, the minerals in the earth and the streams that water the earth. The only reason they have not monopolized the daylight and the air is that it is not possible to do it.
quotes.speaker: Robert Tressell

quotes.text: Much of what is passing for value creation is just value extraction in disguise.
quotes.speaker: Mariana Mazzucato

quotes.text: If money, according to Augier, 'comes into the world with a congenital blood-stain on one cheek,' capital comes dripping from head to foot, from every pore, with blood and dirt.
quotes.speaker: Karl Marx

quotes.text: For thousands of years, violent men have been able to tell their victims that those victims owe them something. If nothing else, they 'owe them their lives' because they haven't been killed.
quotes.speaker: David Graeber

quotes.text: If history shows anything, it is that there's no better way to justify relations founded on violence, to make such relations seem moral, than by reframing them in the language of debt.
quotes.speaker: David Graeber

quotes.text: That amid our highest civilization men faint and die with want is not due to the niggardliness of nature, but to the injustice of man.
quotes.speaker: Henry George

quotes.text: A nation that will keep people in slavery for 244 years will 'thingify' them and make them things. And therefore, they will exploit them and poor people generally economically.
quotes.speaker: Martin Luther King Jr.

quotes.text: There's class warfare, all right, but it's my class, the rich class, that's making war, and we're winning.
quotes.speaker: Warren Buffett
quotes.source: quoted by Ben Stein in "In Class Warfare, Guess Which Class Is Winning," The New York Times, November 26, 2006

quotes.text: The man who dies thus rich dies disgraced.
quotes.speaker: Andrew Carnegie
quotes.source: "The Gospel of Wealth" (originally "Wealth"), North American Review, June 1889

quotes.text: The problem of our age is the proper administration of wealth, so that the ties of brotherhood may still bind together the rich and poor in harmonious relationship.
quotes.speaker: Andrew Carnegie

quotes.text: God gave me my money.
quotes.speaker: John D. Rockefeller Sr.

quotes.text: I believe the power to make money is a gift from God … to be developed and used to the best of our ability for the good of mankind.
quotes.speaker: John D. Rockefeller Sr.

quotes.text: The growth of a large business is merely a survival of the fittest… The American Beauty rose can be produced in the splendor and fragrance which bring cheer to its beholder only by sacrificing the early buds which grow up around it. This is not an evil tendency in business. It is merely the working-out of a law of nature and a law of God.
quotes.speaker: John D. Rockefeller Jr.
quotes.source: address c. 1902 (almost universally misattributed to Rockefeller Sr.)

quotes.text: What has destroyed every previous civilization has been the tendency to the unequal distribution of wealth and power.
quotes.speaker: Henry George

quotes.text: When the rate of return on capital exceeds the rate of growth of output and income, as it did in the nineteenth century and seems quite likely to do again in the twenty-first, capitalism automatically generates arbitrary and unsustainable inequalities that radically undermine the meritocratic values on which democratic societies are based.
quotes.speaker: Thomas Piketty

quotes.text: The idea that unrestricted competition will put an end to inheritance and move toward a more meritocratic world is a dangerous illusion.
quotes.speaker: Thomas Piketty

quotes.text: The upper 1 percent of Americans are now taking in nearly a quarter of the nation's income every year. In terms of wealth rather than income, the top 1 percent control 40 percent.
quotes.speaker: Joseph Stiglitz
quotes.source: "Of the 1%, by the 1%, for the 1%," Vanity Fair, May 2011

quotes.text: The chief enjoyment of riches consists in the parade of riches.
quotes.speaker: Adam Smith
quotes.source: The Wealth of Nations (Bk. I, ch. 11)

quotes.text: The basis on which good repute … ultimately rests is pecuniary strength; and the means of showing pecuniary strength … are leisure and a conspicuous consumption of goods.
quotes.speaker: Thorstein Veblen
quotes.source: The Theory of the Leisure Class

quotes.text: Money is the barometer of a society's virtue.
quotes.speaker: Ayn Rand

quotes.text: Until and unless you discover that money is the root of all good, you ask for your own destruction.
quotes.speaker: Ayn Rand

quotes.text: The only way that I can see to deploy this much financial resource is by converting my Amazon winnings into space travel.
quotes.speaker: Jeff Bezos
quotes.source: interview with Mathias Döpfner (Axel Springer), April 2018

quotes.text: I want to thank every Amazon employee and every Amazon customer, because you guys paid for all of this.
quotes.speaker: Jeff Bezos
quotes.source: press conference after his Blue Origin flight, July 20, 2021

quotes.text: The generic stockholder is a psychopath whose only value is cash return.
quotes.speaker: Doug Sharp

quotes.text: Extraction pulls money upward, always. The only pressures pulling it back toward the people: starvation, chaos, and unions.
quotes.speaker: Doug Sharp

quotes.text: A billionaire needs his seventeenth yacht more than a poor kid needs breakfast. Ask him.
quotes.speaker: Doug Sharp

quotes.text: We must make our choice. We may have democracy, or we may have wealth concentrated in the hands of a few, but we cannot have both.
quotes.speaker: Louis Brandeis
quotes.source: attributed; absent from all his writings per Brandeis archivist Peter Scott Campbell

quotes.text: In a Republican district I was a Republican. In a Democratic district, I was a Democrat. But I was always for Erie.
quotes.speaker: Jay Gould

quotes.text: The public be damned! I am working for my stockholders.
quotes.speaker: William H. Vanderbilt
quotes.source: to reporters aboard his train near Chicago, October 8, 1882

quotes.text: There is one and only one social responsibility of business — to use its resources and engage in activities designed to increase its profits so long as it stays within the rules of the game.
quotes.speaker: Milton Friedman
quotes.source: "The Social Responsibility of Business Is to Increase Its Profits," The New York Times Magazine, September 13, 1970

quotes.text: It may well be that the determination of the government … to punish certain malefactors of great wealth … caused these men to combine to bring about as much financial stress as possible, in order to discredit the policy of the government … so that they may enjoy unmolested the fruits of their own evil-doing.
quotes.speaker: Theodore Roosevelt
quotes.source: address at the Pilgrim Memorial Monument, Provincetown, Mass., August 20, 1907

quotes.text: I regard this contest as one to determine who shall rule this free country—the people through their governmental agents, or a few ruthless and domineering men whose wealth makes them peculiarly formidable because they hide behind the breastworks of corporate organization.
quotes.speaker: Theodore Roosevelt

quotes.text: I look upon the Espionage Law as a despotic enactment in flagrant conflict with democratic principles and with the spirit of free institutions.
quotes.speaker: Eugene V. Debs

quotes.text: Civil government, so far as it is instituted for the security of property, is in reality instituted for the defence of the rich against the poor, or of those who have some property against those who have none at all.
quotes.speaker: Adam Smith

quotes.text: I can hire one half of the working class to kill the other half.
quotes.speaker: Jay Gould
quotes.source: attributed; said to date from the Great Southwest Railroad Strike of 1886

quotes.text: And the hapless Soldier's sigh / Runs in blood down Palace walls.
quotes.speaker: William Blake

quotes.text: To open to civilization the only part of our globe which it has not yet penetrated, to pierce the darkness which hangs over entire peoples, is, I dare say, a crusade worthy of this century of progress.
quotes.speaker: King Leopold II
quotes.source: opening address to the Brussels Geographic Conference, September 12, 1876

quotes.text: I do not want to miss a good chance of getting us a slice of this magnificent African cake.
quotes.speaker: King Leopold II
quotes.source: letter to Baron Solvyns, c. 1877 (as cited in Pakenham, The Scramble for Africa, 1991)

quotes.text: Knights were thugs in tin cans. Heraldry is fancy gang signs.
quotes.speaker: Doug Sharp

quotes.text: British royalty are the spoiled whelps of anointed gangsters.
quotes.speaker: Doug Sharp

quotes.text: The modern conservative is engaged in one of man's oldest, best financed, most applauded, and, on the whole, least successful exercises in moral philosophy. That is the search for a superior moral justification for selfishness.
quotes.speaker: John Kenneth Galbraith
quotes.source: "Wealth and Poverty" address, December 13, 1963 (entered into the Congressional Record)

quotes.text: The marginalist theory of value … justifies excessive inequalities of income and wealth and turns value extraction into value creation.
quotes.speaker: Mariana Mazzucato

quotes.text: But this long run is a misleading guide to current affairs. In the long run we are all dead. Economists set themselves too easy, too useless a task if in tempestuous seasons they can only tell us that when the storm is long past the ocean is flat again.

quotes.text: Debts that can't be paid, won't be paid.

quotes.text: Do not all improvements simply increase the value of land—the price that some must pay others for the privilege of living?
